henry.title: Harvest Dance Rhythms + First Ukulele Strums
henry.intro: Harvest festivals have music with strong beats. First you'll hear beats on the computer, then you'll play a harvest beat on YOUR ukulele and learn your first chord. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: FIRST (2 min): open Chrome Music Lab Rhythm. Tap some dots so they light up, then press ▶. Each lit dot is a drum hit. Count how many you turned on (question 1).
NEXT (10 min): open 'Show me how: Ukulele from zero' below and do steps 1 to 6 with your ukulele. Stuck on the C chord? Watch the video (link 2).
LAST (3 min): fill in the worksheet. You're done when you can play the harvest beat 2 times in a row!
worksheet: How many dots did you light up in Chrome Music Lab Rhythm? ___
Name the 4 ukulele strings from top to bottom (Hint: Green Cows Eat Apples): ___ ___ ___ ___
For the C chord, I press the ___ string with my ___ finger, in fret ___.
Draw a dot where your finger goes for C:
Write the harvest beat with X for strum and - for rest: ___ ___ ___ ___
Which sounded better to you, open strings or the C chord? Circle one: OPEN / C
links: Tap dots to light them up, then press ▶ to hear the monkeys drum.
Video: Beginner Ukulele Lesson for Kids (C chord)
Only if you're stuck: free 6-minute video that shows the strings and the C chord.

handsOn.title: 🎸 Ukulele from zero
steps: guides/uke-strings.svg
Hold it: Sit up. Hug the round body gently against your tummy with your right arm. Your left hand holds the skinny neck like a light handshake.
guides/uke-strings.svg
Meet the strings: From the top string (nearest your face) to the bottom: G, C, E, A. Remember: Green Cows Eat Apples. Pluck each one with your thumb: G… C… E… A.
guides/uke-strings.svg
Strum: Brush your right pointer finger DOWN across all 4 strings over the hole. No left-hand fingers yet, these are 'open strings'. Count 1-2-3-4 and strum on every beat.
guides/uke-strings.svg
Harvest beat: Count out loud 1, 2, 3, 4. Strum DOWN on 1, DOWN on 2, rest (no strum) on 3, DOWN on 4. Written down that's X X - X. Do it 4 times.
guides/uke-c-chord.svg

Your first chord, C: Put the TIP of your left ring finger (finger 3) on the bottom A string, in the 3rd space (fret 3). Press firmly. Pluck the A string: does it ring? Then strum all 4. That's a C chord!
guides/uke-c-chord.svg
Harvest dance with C: Hold the C chord and play the same beat: X X - X. Then let go and play it on open strings. You're done when you can play it 2 times in a row without stopping!
handsOn.look: If a string buzzes, press harder with your fingertip, just behind the fret wire. If it sounds very wrong, the uke may be out of tune: ask a grown-up to tune it with a free tuner app.
handsOn.q: Which string do you press for the C chord, and with which finger?

frankie.title: Falling Leaves on the Piano 🍂
frankie.intro: Leaves fall DOWN from the tree. Let's make music that falls down too, then paint it!
steps: Grown-up: open 'Show me how' below and put stickers (or dots of washable marker or small tape) on 5 piano keys like the picture.
Piano (6 min): Frankie finds the black-key groups, then plays 5-4-3-2-1.
Easel (6 min): grown-up plays the song while Frankie paints falling leaves. Done!
worksheet: Color the leaves to match the dots:
Circle the 2 black keys. Box the 3 black keys.
links: Bonus: draw leaves and tap ▶ to hear them sing!

handsOn.title: 🎹 Piano + 🎨 Easel
steps: guides/piano-leaves.svg
👀 Find the 2 black keys (blue). Find the 3 black keys (purple).
guides/piano-leaves.svg
🏷️ Grown-up: put stickers on 5 white keys: 🔴5 🟠4 🟡3 🟢2 🟤1. The brown 1 is just left of the 2 black keys.
guides/piano-leaves.svg
☝️ Play 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. Leaves falling! 🍂
guides/piano-leaves.svg
🔁 Play it 3 times: slow… slower… sleepy.
guides/piano-leaves.svg
🎨 Easel: paint leaves falling while a grown-up plays the song.
handsOn.look: Grown-up, read aloud. Each key is a leaf: red at the top of the tree, brown on the ground. Say the colors as he plays.
